title: Encode source policy rules and native report ordering
changes: Generate initial native report sorting from complete supported source ORDER BY clauses, with exact direction and NULL placement.
Encode complete conditional assignments, permission resets and overrides, warnings, failure guards and supported local calls as source-bound PL/SQL review code.
Show policy rules awaiting event wiring separately from converted units and retain previous run packages across mapping updates.
limitations: Development preview: source and local checks do not establish a public deployment or completed fresh-customer installation.

Reusable mapping produces an explicit partial synthetic package with read-only reports and supported business rules. Unconverted relationships, transactions and external routines remain listed. Dedicated fresh-installation binding is not yet enabled for this route.

Relationship mapping covers manual read navigation over persisted synthetic rows, not automatic Forms query, dirty buffers or delete lifecycle. Assignment SQL is generated but not installed, Oracle-compiled or event-wired.
Policy review code is not installed, Oracle-compiled or event-wired. Permission effects require server-side enforcement and exact event/state adapters; no new write behavior is activated.

Comparison generation preserves native VARCHAR2/nonpadding under explicit target collation/session prerequisites. Automatic Forms event and duplicate-record workflows are not inferred; runtime equivalence remains unverified.
The deterministic XML path makes no provider calls. Existing AI-backed source processing retains its separate source/destination approvals and does not automatically receive unresolved code.
Format validation is not customer-target import testing, runtime verification or business acceptance; no universal import or behavior guarantee is made.
Supported Oracle Forms tooling, Java and SQLcl remain external prerequisites. Export-only jobs reuse configured provider and compatibility metadata without a live target connection.
The primary new output is an APEXlang ZIP with synthetic supporting SQL and explicit omissions, not a conventional database-derived SQL export.
Measured local protocol-count reductions are not a claimed cloud-model speedup. Dependency-sensitive mapping remains serial; unknown model outcomes are never automatically repeated.
